boards.title: Your First Weekend at Indiana University-Bloomington, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A flexible Saturday-to-Sunday introduction to IU Bloomington through landmarks, green spaces, museums, student gathering places, and a campus cinema.

cards.title: Begin at the Sample Gates
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Kirkwood Avenue entrance
cards.notes: Start beneath the limestone gates, take a campus-arrival photo, then follow the Old Crescent paths east toward the weekend’s next stops.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable starting point where downtown Bloomington meets IU’s historic campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: IU states that the Sample Gates were dedicated in 1987, are made from Indiana limestone, and form an entrance to the Old Crescent.
cards.source_title: History and Milestones of IU Bloomington
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; no specific visiting hours are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Make Room for a Meadow Game
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Dunn Meadow
cards.notes: Bring a frisbee or another simple lawn game, leave room for other visitors, and use this open-air stop to learn a few new names.
cards.short_summary: An informal outdoor pause adds low-pressure movement to the first morning on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: IU’s official first-year bucket list specifically encourages students to play a game in Dunn Meadow.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; the cited page does not provide operating hours or event-specific access rules.

cards.title: Learn the Union’s Layout
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Indiana Memorial Union
cards.notes: Walk through the public lounges, locate the dining and activity areas, and pick a familiar meeting point your group can reuse later.
cards.short_summary: A practical orientation stop inside IU’s central student gathering building.
cards.evidence_claim: IU describes the Indiana Memorial Union as a central campus gathering place with restaurants, lounges, a bowling alley, movies, lectures, and live music.
cards.access_notes: The cited Office of Student Life page lists the IMU at 900 E. Seventh Street and gives building hours of 7 a.m.–midnight; individual services vary.

cards.entity_name: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art
cards.title: Choose One Gallery to Explore Slowly
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Fine Arts Plaza
cards.notes: Pick one gallery instead of rushing the whole museum, read several labels closely, and take only permitted no-flash photographs.
cards.short_summary: A focused gallery visit makes the campus art museum manageable on an already busy weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that admission is always free and that photography is encouraged without flash, tripods, or selfie sticks.
cards.source_title: Your Visit: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours are noon–5 p.m. Tuesday–Sunday, with noon–7 p.m. galleries during First Thursday events; closed Monday.

cards.title: Pause at Showalter Fountain
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Fine Arts Plaza
cards.notes: Step outside after the galleries, circle the fountain for a wider view of the arts buildings, and use the plaza for a group photo.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor visual reset links several major arts destinations on Seventh Street.
cards.evidence_claim: IU’s official Fine Arts Plaza tour map places Showalter Fountain among the Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Auditorium, and Lilly Library destinations.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza feature; fountain operation may vary, and the cited page advises confirming each neighboring destination’s hours.

cards.title: Meet IU’s Special Collections
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Lilly Library
cards.notes: Enter during gallery hours, examine the current display labels, and ask staff how students can responsibly explore special collections later.
cards.short_summary: The first weekend gains a scholarly stop centered on rare books, manuscripts, and cultural records.
cards.evidence_claim: IU identifies the Lilly Library as its Bloomington rare-books, manuscripts, and special-collections library, with holdings across literature, history, science, media, and other fields.
cards.access_notes: The current IU self-guided-tour page lists Monday–Thursday 9:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m., Friday 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m., and Sunday closure; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Check the IU Cinema Marquee
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · IU Auditorium complex
cards.notes: Review the live program before heading over, reserve any required ticket, and arrive early enough to find the north-side entrance calmly.
cards.short_summary: A campus screening offers a structured evening activity without relying on age-restricted nightlife.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Cinema reports screenings four to five days per week during operating periods, usually at 7 p.m., and states that everyone is welcome.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit: Indiana University Cinema
cards.access_notes: IU Cinema closes on campus holidays and for several summer weeks. Screening times and ticket requirements vary, so consult the current program before going.

cards.entity_name: Jesse H. and Beulah Chanley Cox Arboretum
cards.title: Reset in the Cox Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · North-central campus
cards.notes: Take a quiet walk through the arboretum, choose a shaded place to sit, and compare upcoming schedules with your weekend companions.
cards.short_summary: A green-space stop creates an unhurried start before Sunday’s indoor destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: IU’s official first-year bucket list names studying in the Cox Arboretum as a campus experience for students.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landscape; the cited page does not state hours, lighting conditions, or weather-related restrictions.

cards.title: Find Your Library Bearings
cards.subtitle: Sunday midday · Tenth Street and Eagleson Avenue
cards.notes: Locate the reference desk, quiet-study floors, and collaboration areas now so your first assignment does not become a navigation exercise.
cards.short_summary: A short building orientation turns the main library into a usable academic anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: IU identifies Wells Library as the Bloomington library-system hub, with humanities and social-sciences collections, research support, quiet study, and reservable collaboration rooms.
cards.access_notes: Hours change by date; IU Libraries’ current hours page should be checked before departure. Upper stacks close 30 minutes before the building.

cards.entity_name: Indiana University Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology
cards.title: Close with Material Culture
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 416 N. Indiana Avenue
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries with one question in mind: how do objects carry community histories? Record a few exhibits to revisit later.
cards.short_summary: The final stop broadens the weekend from campus navigation to human stories told through objects.
cards.evidence_claim: IUMAA states that it is free and open to all and presents collections connecting Indiana’s First Peoples, contemporary Hoosiers, and societies worldwide.
cards.access_notes: The museum currently lists Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m., Saturday noon–5:30 p.m., and closure Sunday and Monday; move this stop to Saturday when those hours apply.

warnings: The sequence is intentionally flexible: IUMAA is currently closed Sundays, so its card explicitly directs visitors to move that stop to Saturday. IU Cinema programming and ticket prices vary by event.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because exact values were not verified from the cited direct sources.
